blockers: D3 as written breaks the design's own acceptance gate: deleting the adapter-level permission pre-check while reading/parsing the body before dispatch inverts the 403-before-body-parse ordering. examples/shared-contract/src/acceptance.ts:340-419 ('denies missing principals or permissions before every observable effect') sends malformed JSON + wrong permission and requires 403 FORBIDDEN; with lazy body read then dispatch, HttpInputError(INVALID_JSON) fires first and returns 400. packages/adapters-http/src/handler.test.ts:126-166 asserts the same ordering (mapRequest never called on denial). 'Acceptance suite must stay green' fails as designed.

Phase order is self-contradictory with 'npm run verify green at each phase end': D1 (phase 1) deletes defineFeatureContract/define* while compiler (phase 3, scanner.ts keys on those literals), cli (cli.ts:342-346 scaffolds them), testing tests, examples/framework-app, sandbox/notes-app, and benchmarks/runtime/src/benchmark.ts (phase 6) still import them. Verify cannot be green at ends of phases 1-4 unless the old names survive as re-exports until phase 5/6.

D2 'Object.freeze only in dev/test' contradicts an existing production-mode contract test: packages/core/test/application.test.ts:251-252 asserts Object.isFrozen(result.events) and events[0] inside a mode:'production' application. Dropping the deep snapshot+freeze in production also removes the documented anti-aliasing guarantee ('publication is caller-owned') — an execute() retaining the payload reference could mutate an already-emitted event.
amendments: D3: replace the deleted pre-check with a core-exported authorize(operation, principal) (core stays the single authority, no duplicated logic) called by the HTTP handler BEFORE body read/mapRequest; alternatively give dispatch a lazy-input thunk resolved after the permission gate. Either preserves 403-before-body-parse required by acceptance.ts:340-419 and handler.test.ts:126-166.

Order correction: make the deprecated define*/defineFeatureContract re-exports mandatory (not 'if cheap') through phases 1-4; delete them in phase 6 after apps/benchmarks migrate. This is the only way 'verify green at each phase end' holds.

D2: in production keep the structural detach (snapshot) of event payloads and drop only the deep Object.freeze; update application.test.ts:251-252 and the CompletedDispatch doc deliberately. Snapshot cost for typical payloads is sub-microsecond (measured snapshot-bearing dispatch path total 0.64us).

D2: narrow the production validation skip to effect-output re-parse (internal boundary) only. Keep operation output parse and declared-error details parse (external boundary): skipping them turns INVALID_OUTPUT faults into 200s, leaks unstripped keys, and serializes unvalidated error details to the wire — dev/prod divergence. Measured cost of keeping them: ~0.16us per object parse, immaterial vs the 8us HTTP gap.

D2/D5: the v2 single-file rewrite must keep the generated-id guard inside execute (current pattern: framework-app orders/operations.ts:116 OrderId.safeParse(nextId.value.trim())) or exempt random/external-kind port outputs from the production skip — otherwise acceptance 'rejects invalid generated order IDs' fails under production mode. Also run the shared-contract acceptance suite twice (mode test AND production): the factory currently pins mode:'test' (framework-app application.ts:326), so the production fast path is never exercised by the only cross-arm suite.

D3 API shape: createHttpHandler must return an object exposing both the Web fetch entry (edge runtimes, keeps acceptance/node.test contract) and the compiled route table + per-route precomputed status/headers that serveNode drives directly on raw req/res. A bare (Request)=>Promise<Response> handler makes the undici bypass impossible. Rework node.test.ts (91 LOC) with it.

D3 priorities from measurement (share of the ~8us real Express gap): eliminate undici Response construction+arrayBuffer round-trip ~2.7us (~35%), Request construction ~2.4us (~30%), request.json() vs direct JSON.parse of buffered body ~0.6us (~8%), Headers building ~0.6us (~8%), double URL parse ~0.5us (~6%), double body copy (Buffer.concat then Uint8Array.from in node.ts:66) ~0.3us (~4%). Routing scan and the double permission check are ~0 in the echo workload (1 route, empty permission set) — do them for semantics/multi-route scaling, but do not expect benchmark movement from them. Core dispatch is already 0.64us; D2 buys at most ~0.4us here.

Drop schema-compiled serialization from any critical path reasoning: confirmed unnecessary. JSON.stringify of echo-scale payloads is ~0.1us; my D3-style raw-path prototype (no undici, res.end(prestringified), direct dispatch) measured 41.1-43.9us median vs Express 49.0-52.9us and raw-node floor 39.6-42.4us — 'at or below Express median' is realistic with the raw path alone.
